The H125 is the world’s best-selling single-engine helicopter that outclasses other helicopters in its category.
This high-performing versatile helicopter is a member of Airbus’ Ecureuil family, which has accumulated more than 38 million flight hours worldwide.
The proposed helicopter manufacturing facility will be the second FAL to be established in India by Airbus, leveraging TASL’s capabilities in aerospace and defence.

Chandrasekaran, Chairman, Tata Sons, said, “The Tata Group is delighted to set up India’s first helicopter assembly facility in the private sector.

Providing last mile connectivity to remote areas, the H125 will significantly contribute to the Government of India’s regional connectivity scheme – Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik (UDAN) that will further promote the tourism sector in the country.

It can operate in high-and-hot and extreme environments and can be easily reconfigured for various missions, including aerial work, firefighting, law enforcement, rescue, air ambulance, passenger transport, and many others.

The type is known for its high-altitude performance and has seen use by operators in such environments.

The FAL will be the first instance of the private sector setting up a helicopter manufacturing facility in India, providing a major boost to the Government of India’s 'AatmaNirbhar Bharat’ (self-reliant India) programme.
Under this partnership, Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL), a subsidiary of Tata Group, will set up the facility along with Airbus Helicopters.

A ‘Made-in-India’ civil helicopter will not only be a symbol of the confident New India but will also unlock the true potential of the helicopter market in the country,” said Guillaume Faury, Airbus CEO.

“This helicopter final assembly line, which we will build together with our trusted partner Tata, is a reaffirmation of Airbus’ commitment to developing the full spectrum of the aerospace ecosystem in India.
The H125 is the world’s best-selling single-engine helicopter that outclasses other helicopters in its category.
This high-performing versatile helicopter is a member of Airbus’ Ecureuil family, which has accumulated more than 38 million flight hours worldwide.
The proposed helicopter manufacturing facility will be the second FAL to be established in India by Airbus, leveraging TASL’s capabilities in aerospace and defence.
It will also do testing, qualification, and delivery of the H125 to customers in India and the region.
The FAL will take 24 months to set up and deliveries of the first ‘Made in India’ H125s are expected to commence in 2026.
The location of the FAL will be jointly decided by Airbus and the Tata Group.
“Helicopters are crucial for nation building.
This will be the second final assembly line Airbus is building in India after the ‘Make in India’ C295 military aircraft manufacturing facility in Vadodara, Gujarat.” N.
Chandrasekaran, Chairman, Tata Sons, said, “The Tata Group is delighted to set up India’s first helicopter assembly facility in the private sector.

Providing last mile connectivity to remote areas, the H125 will significantly contribute to the Government of India’s regional connectivity scheme – Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik (UDAN) that will further promote the tourism sector in the country.

It can operate in high-and-hot and extreme environments and can be easily reconfigured for various missions, including aerial work, firefighting, law enforcement, rescue, air ambulance, passenger transport, and many others.

The latest announcement is part of Airbus’ efforts to develop a holistic aerospace ecosystem in India, where the company is expanding its industrial footprint with aircraft assembly, component manufacturing, engineering and digital design and development, MRO support, pilot and maintenance training as well as academic collaboration to foster human capital.

All photos Summary When to go Getting there Top cities Regions Destinations Best locations Attractions Landmarks About Best time to go Map Tickets & tours Nearby Neighbourhoods Hotels Restaurants Bars Essentials Phrases History Nearby cities Nearby destinations Nearby neighbourhoods Neighbouring countries Nearby regions Keeneland in Lexington, Kentucky, pairs famed Thoroughbred racing with horse-country landscapes, historic barns, race-day traditions and easy airport access. Racing Country on the City’s Edge Keeneland is less a conventional urban neighbourhood than a distinctive rural-urban landscape on Lexington’s south-western edge, organised around Keeneland Race Course and the broad approaches to Blue Grass Airport. The area sits along Versailles Road amid paddocks, limestone fences, horse farms, mature trees and low-density development, offering a markedly different experience from central Lexington’s streets and commercial districts. Its identity is inseparable from the Thoroughbred industry that shapes the wider Bluegrass region, but Keeneland preserves that connection in a particularly visible form. Read more about Keeneland The Racecourse and Its Setting Keeneland Race Course is the area’s defining attraction, with a celebrated autumn and spring racing calendar, landscaped grounds and a visual language of white fencing, brick, timber and carefully maintained turf. On non-race days, the grounds can feel measured and spacious, while race meetings bring spectators, horse owners, trainers and long-standing local rituals to the grandstand and paddock. The nearby Keeneland Library adds depth to the experience through its research collections on racing, breeding and equestrian history. PHOTO: AFP Published Nov 01, 2026, 07:46 PM Updated Nov 01, 2026, 07:46 PM Set as preferred source LEXINGTON, Kentucky – Sovereignty took out the US$7 million (S$8.94 million) Grade 1 Breeders’ Cup Classic (2,000m) at Keeneland on Oct 31, denying Japan’s Forever Young a rare repeat in the showpiece of the racing extravaganza. Trained by US Hall of Fame trainer Bill Mott and ridden by Junior Alvarado, the 2025 dual-Grade 1 Kentucky Derby (2,000m) and Belmont Stakes (2,000m) winner seized his first chance in the famous race after he was scratched from last year’s edition because of a fever. The Into Mischief four-year-old was beaten twice at his 2026 campaign when he finished second in the Grade 2 Oaklawn Handicap (1,800m) at Oaklawn Park on April 19 and third in the Grade 1 Stephen Foster Stakes (1,800m) at Churchill Downs on June 28. But the talented galloper went on to land the Grade 1 Whitney Stakes (1,800m) at Saratoga on Aug 9 last start. This time, his Classic participation was again threatened by a hoof abscess, but Alvarado said he never doubted that Sovereignty could win the Classic. “What he did today, Sovereignty, it’s just spectacular,” said the Venezuelan jockey. “We really wanted to run so bad the Classic last year. tool.excerpt: In his second start at Aqueduct in September, he was beaten by a neck. At the end of October, trainer Bill Mott sent Sovereignty into stakes company at Churchill Downs in the Grade III Street Sense Stakes over a distance of 1+1⁄16 miles. Leaving the gate a step slow and spotting the field in last place, Sovereignty rallied on the outside through the Churchill stretch and drew away to win by five lengths. === 2025: three-year-old season === Sovereignty was rested until March, when Godolphin and Mott entered him in the three-year-old Kentucky Derby prep races at Gulfstream Park in Florida. His first race of 2025 was the Grade II Fountain of Youth Stakes, in which he again trailed the field before moving up around the turn and down the short stretch of Gulfstream's 1+1⁄16-mile racing configuration, defeating River Thames by a neck. ... Sovereignty (foaled February 22, 2022) is an American retired Thoroughbred racehorse. He won multiple graded stakes races, most notable the 2025 Kentucky Derby, Belmont Stakes, Travers Stakes, and the 2026 Breeders' Cup Classic. Sovereignty became the first horse to win two legs of the American Triple Crown (the Kentucky Derby and the Belmont Stakes) since Justify swept all three Triple Crown races in 2018. == Background == Sovereignty is owned by Godolphin, the thoroughbred stables whose proprietor is Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the Emir of Dubai. tool.excerpt: The 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix (officially known as the Formula 1 Gran Premio de la Ciudad de México 2026) was a Formula One motor race that was held on 1 November 2026 at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City, Mexico. Antonelli became the youngest Drivers' Champion at the age of 20 years, two months and seven days, beating the previous record holder Sebastian Vettel, the first Italian Drivers' Champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, and Mercedes' first Drivers' Championship since Hamilton secured his seventh title in 2020. Ahead of him, Max Verstappen (Red Bull) won the race and Hamilton finished second in an eventful race. The Grand Prix also saw Ryo Hirakawa make his Formula One Grand Prix debut with Haas, where he benefitted from drivers ahead of him receiving penalties to score his first Formula One point. == Background == The event was held at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City for the 26th time in the circuit's history, across the weekend of 30 October – 1 November, having previously held twenty editions of the Mexican Grand Prix. The Grand Prix was the ninteenth round of the 2026 Formula One World Championship and the sixth held under the name of the Mexico City Grand Prix, having previously been titled the Mexican Grand Prix. === Championship standings before the race === Going into the weekend, Kimi Antonelli led the Drivers' Championship with 365 points, 123 points ahead of teammate George Russell in second and 124 ahead of Lewis Hamilton in third. Mercedes, with 607 points, led the Constructors' Championship from Ferrari, who were second with 474 points, and Red Bull and McLaren, who both tied on 355 points. ==== Championship permutations ==== Going into the race, there were 125 points available across the five remaining scheduled rounds. It was the nineteenth round of the 2026 Formula One World Championship. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) took his first pole position since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, and his first pole position with the team. Kimi Antonelli clinched his first Formula One World Drivers' Championship after achieving third. Antonelli became the youngest Drivers' Champion at the age of 20 years, two months and seven days, beating the previous record holder Sebastian Vettel, the first Italian Drivers' Champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, and Mercedes' first Drivers' Championship since Hamilton secured his seventh title in 2020. Ahead of him, Max Verstappen (Red Bull) won the race and Hamilton finished second in an eventful race. The Grand Prix also saw Ryo Hirakawa make his Formula One Grand Prix debut with Haas, where he benefitted from drivers ahead of him receiving penalties to score his first Formula One point. == Background == The event was held at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City for the 26th time in the circuit's history, across the weekend of 30 October – 1 November, having previously held twenty editions of the Mexican Grand Prix. The Grand Prix was the ninteenth round of the 2026 Formula One World Championship and the sixth held under the name of the Mexico City Grand Prix, having previously been titled the Mexican Grand Prix. === Championship standings before the race === Going into the weekend, Kimi Antonelli led the Drivers' Championship with 365 points, 123 points ahead of teammate George Russell in second and 124 ahead of Lewis Hamilton in third. Mercedes, with 607 points, led the Constructors' Championship from Ferrari, who were second with 474 points, and Red Bull and McLaren, who both tied on 355 points. ==== Championship permutations ==== Going into the race, there were 125 points available across the five remaining scheduled rounds. It was the nineteenth round of the 2026 Formula One World Championship. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) took his first pole position since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, and his first pole position with the team. Kimi Antonelli clinched his first Formula One World Drivers' Championship after achieving third. Antonelli became the youngest Drivers' Champion at the age of 20 years, two months and seven days, beating the previous record holder Sebastian Vettel, the first Italian Drivers' Champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, and Mercedes' first Drivers' Championship since Hamilton secured his seventh title in 2020. Ahead of him, Max Verstappen (Red Bull) won the race and Hamilton finished second in an eventful race. The Grand Prix also saw Ryo Hirakawa make his Formula One Grand Prix debut with Haas, where he benefitted from drivers ahead of him receiving penalties to score his first Formula One point. == Background == The event was held at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City for the 26th time in the circuit's history, across the weekend of 30 October – 1 November, having previously held twenty editions of the Mexican Grand Prix. The Grand Prix was the ninteenth round of the 2026 Formula One World Championship and the sixth held under the name of the Mexico City Grand Prix, having previously been titled the Mexican Grand Prix. === Championship standings before the race === Going into the weekend, Kimi Antonelli led the Drivers' Championship with 365 points, 123 points ahead of teammate George Russell in second and 124 ahead of Lewis Hamilton in third. The violence comes after the Group of Seven (G7) sounded the alarm on Wednesday over the “recent escalation of violence” in Sudan’s war, which erupted more than two and a half years ago. The war between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has killed tens of thousands of people, displaced nearly 12 million more and triggered one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises. The violence has escalated dramatically in recent weeks, with the RSF seizing control of the key town of El-Fasher and with reports of atrocities multiplying. Merowe is in an area that has been under army control for months. The town, about 330 kilometers (200 miles) north of the capital Khartoum, was plunged into darkness after a full power cut, witnesses told AFP . The RSF has increasingly resorted to drones in recent months, though the military also uses drones to conduct strikes.
